content:
Alice S.: FYI customer 'GreenTech' hit a returned ACH — bank rejected the transfer citing an invalid routing suffix. Pasting payload and bank reply below, please triage. @Maria P.

payments-bot: created incident INC-4521 for thread (priority: high) :rotating_light:

Alice S.: tx_id: GT-2024-09-17-7312
Alice S.: payment payload (sanitized):
```json
{
  "amount": 36250,
  "currency": "USD",
  "beneficiary": { "name": "GreenTech Ops", "account_number": "987654321" },
  "routing_number": "123456789US",
  "payment_method": "ach"
}
```

Alice S.: bank response (ACH gateway):
```
REJECT: invalid_routing_number_suffix - destination bank flagged routing '123456789US' as malformed
ReturnCode: R10
Message: routing contains non-numeric suffix
```

Maria P.: thanks. Was this initiated via Hosted API or Dedicated?

Alice S.: Dedicated pool (customer uses reserved capacity). No intermediate transforms on our side AFAIK.

Sam G.: quick glance: routing_number should be 9 digits for ABA. Looks like an alpha suffix got appended upstream. Can you confirm the raw request from the client?

Alice S.: client says they uploaded a CSV and we ingested it. Sending the CSV row they uploaded:
```
GreenTech Ops,987654321,123456789-US
```

Sam G.: aha — CSV had hyphen + country code. Our intake normalizer currently strips spaces and punctuation but preserves trailing alpha tokens. So we forwarded '123456789US' to the payment runtime. Bank rejects.

Kyle R.: Repro steps for eng: spin up local env and run this curl (mirrors ingestion path):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/payments \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d '{"beneficiary": {"name":"GreenTech Ops","account_number":"987654321"},"routing_number":"123456789US","amount":36250,"currency":"USD","payment_method":"ach"}'
```

Sam G.: thanks. I can reproduce the reject in staging (gateway returns same error). Proposed fix: update CSV/ingest normalizer to drop any non-digit chars and then validate length==9 before accepting. If not 9 digits, respond 400 with clear error to client. Also add a conversion step to remove common country suffixes (US, CA) that are accidentally appended.

Maria P.: agree. Add a monitoring alert for 'routing_normalization_failures' so we can catch bulk bad uploads. Also need a message template to send to GreenTech about corrected format and next steps.

Kyle R.: I'll open a PR to the normalizer service and add unit tests + a small integration test against our ACH gateway stub. Plan to roll to staging within the hour.

Sam G.: patch LGTM, tests added. Deployed to staging and ran the curl above — now we return 400 with body:
```json
{ "error": "invalid_routing_number", "detail": "routing_number must be 9 digits after normalization" }
```

Maria P.: notify ops to hold mass re-ingest until we patch production. I'll draft the customer note.

Alice S.: customer update sent: explained cause, asked them to re-upload CSV after stripping suffixes or let us run a one-time cleanup.

payments-bot: INC-4521 status -> in_progress (assignee: Kyle R.)

Kyle R.: patch merged and rolling to prod now (canary 10%). Will monitor for errors.

Sam G.: after canary looks good, schedule full rollout + backfill job to reprocess today's CSVs for affected accounts. Backfill will normalize routing and queue retries only for rows that validate to 9 digits.

Kyle R.: canary healthy for 12m, no new rejects. Rolling full deploy.

payments-bot: INC-4521 status -> resolved by Kyle R. (fix deployed)

Alice S.: Customer confirmed successful retry after we corrected the routing and reprocessed — marking this thread resolved from support side. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Maria P.: follow-up item: add a console warning when users upload CSVs with non-digit routing fields. Filed UX ticket UX-621.

Sam G.: filing postmortem checklist items: add automated fuzz test for routing normalization and add observability on normalized vs raw routing counts.

Alice S.: closing the loop. Great cross-team response.
